subject: Request: VPC affinity/failover carveout for latency SLO (SummitEdge)
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@summitedge.io>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@summitedge.io>, Sophie Leung <sophie.leung@summitedge.io>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: VPC affinity/failover carveout for latency SLO

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — SummitEdge is excited about migrating low-latency inference to Redwood Private. Before we finalize the procurement paperwork, our networking team flagged a risk: our colo uses active-active peering to a single transit provider in us-west-2 and we intentionally maintain affinity to a local POP to minimize hop count. If that path experiences loss we fail traffic to an alternate POP which can add 60–150ms at the TCP level. For our real-time inference workload that exceeds the 50ms latency SLO you shared.

We'd like to request an SLA carveout or attribution rule that treats failures caused by SummitEdge-controlled WAN peering (including BGP flap, transit provider congestion, or colo cross-connect impairment) as customer-controlled events for latency SLOs, rather than Redwood infrastructure faults. We can provide traceroutes, router dumps, and a runbook to prove ownership.

Can you advise on what evidence you need and how to document this in the SLA/appendix? We want minimal operational surprise but still need clear uptime/latency commitments for the service.

Attached is a simplified network diagram and our default failover playbook.

Oliver
Head of Platform Engineering
SummitEdge

Attachments: summitedge-network-topology.pdf

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@summitedge.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: VPC affinity/failover carveout for latency SLO

Oliver —

Thanks for the clear note and the diagram, that helps. Short answer: we can consider an attribution carveout that excludes SummitEdge-managed WAN/transit events from Redwood latency SLO calculations, but we need a reproducible evidence protocol, a labeled appendix to the SLA, and operational hooks so we can verify incidents quickly.

High-level ask from our side:
- A binding runbook that describes detection, ownership, and escalation (who runs traceroutes, who opens transit provider tickets).
- Regular telemetry access (NetFlow/traceroute dumps) for post-incident attributions.
- Agreement on a rolling sample window (e.g., 5m/1h buckets) for how latency breaches are evaluated when failover occurs.
- Optional: a joint on-call rotation for the initial 90 days.

I'll loop in Karthik and Naomi to outline the draft SLA language and the evidence list. If Procurement needs pricing concessions for the carveout we can put that in the commercial annex.

Best,
Mateo
Customer Success (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: VPC affinity/failover carveout for latency SLO

Naomi / Mateo —

Drafting notes for the legal/compliance side. We should avoid broad, permanent carveouts. Proposed structure:
1) "Customer-Controlled Network Events" definition that lists: BGP route changes initiated by customer's ASN, colo cross-connect physical faults with customer ticket evidence, and third-party transit provider capacity exhaustion with provider notification.
2) Evidence required: traceroute (pre/post), time-stamped NetFlow summary, provider ticket reference, and runbook excerpt showing active failover. Evidence must be submitted within 72 hours of incident detection.
3) Limited-term pilot: 6-month trial window where attributions are logged but final SLA credit decisions are reversible pending joint review.
4) Telemetry: SummitEdge to grant read-only access to specific telemetry buckets (S3/Drive link) for incident windows only.

Also recommend a clause that requires SummitEdge to maintain symmetric peering and to notify Redwood prior to any planned BGP/peering changes. Failure to notify should reduce carveout applicability.

Jonas — can you confirm whether the runtime can tag and exclude tokens from latency SLO calcs when we detect customer-edge failover? We need a technical control to stop counting affected requests.

Karthik
Head of Legal (Commercial Contracts)
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 31 Mar 2028 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: VPC affinity/failover carveout for latency SLO

Karthik —

Technically feasible with constraints. We can create an "attribution flag" in our telemetry pipeline: when an incident ticket is opened and evidence is uploaded, the ingestion pipeline will tag requests originating from SummitEdge's VPCs in the incident time window. Tagged requests can be excluded from latency percentiles/SLI reporting. Caveats:
- Tags are retroactive only to the start of the ingestion window; very short incidents (<30s) may not be fully captured.
- Requires SummitEdge to push a short incident manifest (start/end timestamps + evidence link) to a signed endpoint we expose.
- There will be a small cost to retain higher-resolution telemetry for attorney review.

I'll prototype the manifest endpoint for the pilot and coordinate with infra on SLO exclusion logic.

Jonas
SRE, Redwood Runtime

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@summitedge.io>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Leung <sophie.leung@summitedge.io>, Procurement <procurement@summitedge.io>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: VPC affinity/failover carveout for latency SLO

Mateo / Karthik / Jonas —

This approach looks reasonable. We can commit to the runbook + evidence protocol (traceroute snapshots, provider ticket, and timestamps). For the pilot window, SummitEdge will grant read-only access to the telemetry S3 path for incident windows and will provide a signed manifest as you request.

One ask from our side: during the pilot, we need explicit language that non-attributable infra outages (Redwood cluster failures, kernel panics, regional fabric issues) remain fully covered by Redwood SLOs and are not impacted by the carveout. We don't want the carveout to be interpreted to dilute Redwood's responsibilities.

I'll attach our standard failover runbook and a redline to the proposed SLA addendum by EOD.

Oliver

Attachments: proposed-sla-addendum-draft.docx, evidence-edge-runbook.zip

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@summitedge.io>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: VPC affinity/failover carveout for latency SLO

Thanks everyone —

I'll combine Karthik's language and Jonas's technical control notes into a single SLA appendix draft and circulate a redline by Thursday. Key decisions to include in the draft:
- Customer-Controlled Network Events definition (enumerated).
- Evidence submission timeline (72 hours) and manifest format (start/end + S3 link + provider ticket id).
- Pilot period: 6 months with monthly joint reviews; final carveout adoption subject to review.
- Non-attribution clause reiterating Redwood's full responsibility for platform and regional infra faults.
- Pricing/credit treatment: commercial to propose whether a small monthly operations fee or alternative pricing applies for the telemetry retention and joint on-call.

Mateo: please confirm if Procurement should be looped for commercial tradeoffs now or after the draft.

Best —
Naomi
Director, Product Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
